subject: Request: Exec approval for strategic hosted API usage rebate — PioneerHealth

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: PioneerHealth - ask for exec approval on usage rebate

Laura,

Quick heads-up: PioneerHealth (Alex Jenkins) came back after today's commercial call asking for a "strategic usage rebate" that would effectively reduce our Hosted API per-token rates by 28% starting at the committed volume band. They are planning a 12-month committed usage with an aggressive ramp: attached is their forecast.

Why this is on your desk: the ask exceeds our 20% standard discount authority and they are requesting a rebate that applies retroactively to month 1 of the commitment if they hit the volume milestones. They've mentioned a pilot running in production by July and a multi-year procurement process contingent on this concession.

Key facts: 
- Proposed effective discount: 28% on Hosted API usage at the committed tier
- Initial committed spend: ~$850k ARR (YR1) with potential to double in YR2 conditional on success
- Customer is sensitive to vendor consolidation; they want demonstrable unit cost parity with incumbent
- They asked for a short signature timeline (2 weeks) to include in procurement packet

Attachments: usage_forecast_Q3_Q4.xlsx (Ben)

Can you advise if we can escalate for exec clearance? Jonas, any capacity or SLA flags on your end?

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Fwd: PioneerHealth - ask for exec approval on usage rebate

Thanks Laura/Ben — I reviewed the forecast. A few items to proceed: 

1) Confirmed ARR profile and payment terms (upfront vs monthly). We can consider a deeper rebate if they do >60% upfront.
2) Minimum commitment and true-up cadence (quarterly true-ups or annual?). Retroactive rebates are tricky — prefer forward-looking credits only.
3) Margin impact: at 28% it looks like our contribution margin on this account drops below our 55% target at projected usage; need a plan to offset (e.g., usage floor, minimum MSR).

If Ben can secure a 12-month minimum with 3-month ramp guardrails and 60% upfront, I can support a rebate up to 30% as a one-time exec concession, provided legal signs off on non-retroactivity and we add an early-termination recovery clause.

Marking this tentative approval with conditions — remove retroactivity, secure payment cadence, include recovery on early termination.

Mina

VP, Finance | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: PioneerHealth - ask for exec approval on usage rebate

Looping legal considerations: 

- We need to avoid language that creates an ongoing entitlement to the rebate beyond the contracted term. I recommend: rebate as a one-time billing credit tied to milestone attestation and payment receipt.
- Retroactive application to month 1 must be rejected unless Procurement offers a signed, irrevocable commitment with a true financial guarantee.
- Suggest adding: recovery clause for early termination (pro-rated clawback), audit rights for usage verification, and a cap on maximum aggregate credit.

I will draft redline language for the master services agreement (MSA) and SOW once we confirm the commercial parameters.

Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Exec clearance: PioneerHealth strategic usage rebate (approved with conditions)

Ben — good work pulling the forecast and commitment. After review Mina has agreed to provide exec clearance on a one-time strategic usage rebate up to 25% (not 28%) provided you secure the following from PioneerHealth by EOD Friday 5/14: 

1) Signed 12-month commitment (Deal ID PH-2027-0428) with the committed minimum spend of no less than $850k ARR and an explicit usage ramp schedule.
2) Payment terms: 60% upfront prepay for year 1, remainder monthly. Upfront payment must be processed before credits apply.
3) Rebate mechanics: one-time billing credit applied after month 3 milestone confirmation; no retroactive credits to month 1.
4) Contract language: Rishi to produce redline including clawback on early termination and audit rights. Ben — share the signed SOW and procurement contact so I can loop procurement for timeline.

Jonas — ops confirmation: are there any capacity/SLA caveats if they ramp faster than forecast?

Once the paperwork meets the conditions we will execute the concession and I will sign off. This gives us headroom to protect margin while enabling the strategic reference.

Laura
